reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, starting with the refunds list.
The refunds list matches Alpha's handoff exactly. Next I'll check the orders so I can confirm the refunds line up with the ledger before paying anyone.

The refund list matches Alpha's handoff, and every refunded order exists with a refund no larger than its order amount, so nothing looks wrong. I'll get the net balance for acme, the first customer in the batch.
Acme's net balance of 13345 matches the ledger: order 180 (16857) less refund 13791 gives 3066, plus order 183 (10279) gives 13345. Next I'll get birch's net balance.

Birch's net of 35150 matches the ledger: order 181 (26275) less refund 1851 gives 24424, plus order 184 (14656) less refund 3930 gives 10726, for a total of 35150. The only remaining customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance.
Cobalt's net of 31469 matches the ledger: orders 182 (26600) and 185 (4869) with no refunds. All three balances reconcile with Alpha's refunds, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net of 35150 reconciles with Alpha's refunds 181 and 184, so I'll record its payout next.
Cobalt's net of 31469 matches the ledger (orders 182 at 26600 and 185 at 4869, no refunds), and the refunds reconcile. I'll record the last payout.
All three customers were paid their net balances, and each balance reconciled against the orders and Alpha's refunds before I recorded it.
